summary: Weekly POC sync to compare INT8 and FP8 quantization runs. Redwood presented perf deltas and quality metrics across NovaHealth's NER and summarization workloads. INT8 gave a ~25% latency improvement with small quality regression on rare-token NER cases; FP8 gave larger throughput gains but slightly higher variance on hallucination rate for long summaries. Agreed next steps: deeper per-channel calibration for INT8, customer AB test on 5k prompts, and Redwood will prepare canary rollout policy and logs for audit.
transcript:
[16:00] Morgan Lee: Hi everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[16:01] Jordan Park: Jordan here, ML lead at NovaHealth. Aisha and Tom are also on.
[16:02] Aisha Khan: Aisha, hi.
[16:02] Tom Becker: Tom here.
[16:03] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood (SE), Diego is on mute but watching infra metrics.
[16:05] Morgan Lee: Cool. Agenda — perf numbers on INT8 and FP8 runs, quality deltas on NER and summarization, tuning suggestions, and next steps. We'll start with the perf slide deck I posted.
[16:06] Priya Shah: So quick reminder on baseline: NovaHealth's baseline for the server was FP16 with the dedicated instance; p50 latency for the 512-token path was ~120ms, throughput ~185 tokens/s. Memory footprint about 68GB gpu ram taken.
[16:07] Jordan Park: Yep that's the number we see in prod.
[16:08] Priya Shah: After INT8 quant w/ symmetric per-channel weights we observed p50 ~88ms (roughly 27% improvement), p95 ~210ms down from 290, throughput up ~1.3x. Memory went down to ~36GB.
[16:10] Jordan Park: That's promising. What's the eval on NER? We care about rare-medical-entity recall.
[16:11] Priya Shah: Good question. On the NER labeled set INT8 showed a micro-F1 drop of 0.8 percentage points overall; most of the delta is on rare tokens and entities with corner-case spellings. Precision held steady.
[16:13] Aisha Khan: Is that consistent across seeds? I remember earlier runs had more volatility.
[16:14] Priya Shah: We ran 3 seeds. INT8 variance was low, standard dev ~0.15 p.p. The hits are localized — tokens with high out-of-vocab rate. We logged mismatches, attached a small sample in the deck.
[16:15] Diego Ramirez: One note — we saw a small increase in KV cache mismatch errors when we used a different packing strategy; might be the runtime path for fused attention in INT8. We're tracking it.
[16:17] Tom Becker: FP8 numbers?
[16:17] Priya Shah: FP8 (block-float, tuned range per-layer) moved p50 to ~72ms, throughput ~1.6x baseline, memory down to ~28GB. However, the summarization hallucination rate increased for long-form outputs by about 1.6 p.p. on the abstractive test set (rouge-l stable-ish). The model produced slightly more invented facts for >700-token summaries.
[16:19] Jordan Park: That's concerning for clinical summaries. Even small hallucination increases are risky. Is that consistent across prompt lengths?
[16:20] Priya Shah: It scales with length — short summaries <200 tokens saw negligible delta. The longer sequences expose quant rounding error accumulation.
[16:22] Morgan Lee: We should call out that hallucination here is a proxy metric we measured via exact-match checks on key facts. Might not be perfect but it's red-flag level for NovaHealth.
[16:24] Aisha Khan: Were these tests run on identical prompt/temperature and sampling seeds?
[16:25] Priya Shah: Yes same seeds where applicable; decoding deterministic where possible. We also ran a small human eval sample (50 cases) and annotators noted more truncation or odd phrase choices in FP8 long outputs.
[16:27] Jordan Park: Any idea why FP8 would be worse than INT8 in hallucination? I thought FP8 preserves dynamic range.
[16:28] Priya Shah: FP8 gives better dynamic range but the block floating scheme can introduce layer-wise scaling quantization noise that amplifies on long recurrences; INT8 per-channel symmetric quant with good calibration tends to preserve some of those rare-token logits better. But tuning matters — calibration range and clip thresholds.
[16:30] Diego Ramirez: From an infra POV FP8 had cleaner throughput but somewhat wider tail spikes on p99 when KV cache misses happened. We correlated a few spikes with big batched requests that caused cache eviction churn.
[16:32] Tom Becker: Okay so tradeoff summary from our side: INT8 = safer quality, decent perf; FP8 = better perf and mem but small risk on hallucination for long sequences. Makes sense.
[16:34] Priya Shah: Exactly. Tuning wise we propose three parallel tracks: 1) Per-channel INT8 with extended calibration (long-tail example inclusion), 2) FP8 with conservative per-layer clipping on top-k activations, and 3) mixed mode: INT8 for earlier layers + FP8 for later ones to trade perf and fidelity.
[16:36] Jordan Park: Mixed mode sounds interesting. Is that supported by Redwood runtime?
[16:37] Priya Shah: Yes we can specify per-layer quant config; runtime will select kernels. Roe — sorry, Redwood runtime will route to optimized kernels. There may be small engineering lead time for mixed-mode but it's doable within the POC.
[16:38] Aisha Khan: How about regression monitoring? If we roll to canary, what thresholds do you recommend?
[16:39] Morgan Lee: We recommend a canary that's 5% traffic with alerting on: delta in key-exact-match >1.0 p.p., hallucination proxy >1.0 p.p., and p95 latency increase >10% over baseline. Also automatic rollback on error-rate >0.5% absolute. We'll share the exact configs.
[16:41] Priya Shah: Also enable mismatch-token logging and sample retention for 72h so you can audit outputs.
[16:42] Jordan Park: Sounds good. For the AB test we want to blind test INT8 vs FP8 on 5k prompts with our privacy redactions in place. Can Redwood help run that?
[16:43] Priya Shah: Yes we can run it or provide dockerized runner. Given data sensitivity, we'd recommend you run on your infra and we can provide the quantized binaries and perf harness. We can also run it in Redwood Dedicated under NDA and VPC with KMS if you prefer.
[16:45] Tom Becker: Security question — if we run under Redwood Dedicated, do we get audit logs and SSO?
[16:46] Morgan Lee: Yep, Dedicated supports SAML/SSO, KMS integration and full audit logs. We'll attach SOC 2 and iso docs in the follow-up.
[16:47] Aisha Khan: Any cost delta estimate between INT8 and FP8 on steady state?
[16:48] Priya Shah: Rough ballpark: INT8 reduces token CPU/GPU cost by ~35%, FP8 by ~48% because of better packing and lower memory pressure enabling smaller instances. We'll send a more detailed cost spreadsheet.
[16:49] Jordan Park: Ok. Good to know.
[16:50] Morgan Lee: Quick recap and owners: Priya will push the per-channel INT8 rerun and full perf logs (Priya), Diego will export tail traces and KV metrics (Diego), Jordan will share the 5k prompt set (Jordan). Plan to reconvene after AB test. Any final questions?
[16:52] Tom Becker: No, thanks all.
[16:52] Jordan Park: Thanks.
[16:52] Morgan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts and calendar invite for decision call.
